memory_versions.text:
**Campaign Working Notes (as of Day 10)**

**Pooled result:** 4 of last 10 pushes landed. First positive delta (+0.40) came from angle B (quality story) on Day 10.

**Angle performance so far:**
- C (urgency): pushed 5× (days 2, 4, 5, 6, 7) — all +0.00. Clearly over-rotated. Stop leading with this.
- B (quality story): pushed 3× (days 1, 3, 9, 10) — one hit. Best-performing angle so far.
- D (testimonial): pushed 1× (day 8) — +0.00. Small sample, no signal yet.
- A (price cut): pushed 0×. Untested.

**Key takeaways:**
- Urgency fatigue is real. Five straight C pushes produced nothing. Audience didn't respond to repeated countdown/pressure framing.
- B (quality/story) is the current winner. It aligns with "arm enough to handle a narrative-forward push without feeling jarring" — the audience is still in a trust-building phase, not a decision phase.
- No per-day breakdown available, so can't isolate which of the 4 landed pushes were which angle. Assume B contributed given it was the only one with a positive delta.

**List health:**
- Steady small growth (days 5, 6, 8).
- Two unsubscribes processed Day 1. No deliverability complaints through Day 10.
- Legal signed off on all four angles.

**Next-cycle plan:**
- Lead with B or D for the next 3–4 days. Let the narrative/testimonial do the work.
- Hold C in reserve; revisit only if the audience shows clear purchase-intent signals (e.g., spike in CTR on B pushes).
- Consider testing A (price cut) once — it's the one untried angle and the audience may be past curiosity.
- Watch for the next pooled report to confirm whether the B/D shift sustains lift.

**Send window:** 10am daily, confirmed reliable.

**Campaign Working Notes (as of Day 20)**

**Pooled result:** 4 of last 10 pushes landed (same as Day 10 report). The single visible positive delta in this window came from D (testimonial) on Day 20 (+0.40).

**Angle performance, Days 11–20:**
- D (testimonial): 7 pushes (days 12, 13, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20) — one hit (+0.40 on day 20). First positive delta ever for D, but came after six zeros. Pattern: D seems to need repetition to land.
- B (quality story): 2 pushes (days 11, 14) — 0/2. Day 10's hit did not repeat. B's lead may have been a one-off or the audience has moved past narrative framing.
- A (price cut): 1 push (day 16) — 0/1. First test, no signal.
- C (urgency): 0 pushes. Held in reserve as planned. Still unused since Day 7.

**Key takeaways:**
- D is now the best-performing angle. The strategy of leading with D for multiple days was correct in hindsight — it needed six attempts before landing.
- B's Day 10 hit was likely a one-off or the audience has outgrown pure narrative.
- A is unproven. One data point is insufficient; revisit if a second test is warranted.
- C has been untouched for 13 days. If D sustains, C may never be needed. If D stalls, C is the fallback for urgency-driven conversion.
- No per-day breakdown available; cannot confirm which of the 4 "landed" pushes correspond to which angles. Assume D contributed given it's the only one with a visible delta.

**List health:**
- 4 unsubscribes total (2 on Day 1, 2 on Day 11, 2 on Day 19). Small rate but trending slightly upward. Monitor.
- List grew on Days 15 and 18.
- No deliverability complaints through Day 20.
- Legal signed off on all four angles (confirmed Day 13).

**Next-cycle plan:**
- Continue leading with D. It has proven it can land when given enough reps.
- Hold A in reserve for a second test if D plateaus.
- Keep C as a last-resort lever; do not reintroduce until a clear purchase-intent spike or a stall in D.
- Watch unsubscribe rate — 4 in 20 days is tolerable, but if it accelerates, audit D's content for tone mismatch.

**Send window:** 10am daily, confirmed reliable.

**Campaign Working Notes (as of Day 30)**

**Pooled result:** 3 of last 10 pushes landed (down from 4 on Day 20). Two visible positive deltas in the full window: D on Day 20 (+0.40) and D on Day 30 (+0.30).

**Angle performance, Days 21–30:**
- D (testimonial): 9 pushes (days 21–27, 29, 30) — one hit (+0.30 on Day 30). Eight consecutive zeros (Days 21–27, 29) before the next land. Pattern confirms: D requires long streaks of reps before it connects. Cumulative D record: 16 pushes, 2 hits ≈ 12.5%.
- C (urgency): 1 push (Day 28) — 0/1. First test since Day 7. No signal yet; single data point.
- A (price cut): 0 pushes this window. Cumulative: 1 push (Day 16), 0 hits.
- B (quality story): 0 pushes this window. Cumulative: 2 pushes, 0 hits. Effectively retired from active rotation.

**Key takeaways:**
- D is the only angle that has ever landed twice. Its hit rate is low (~1 in 5–8) but the payoff when it lands is real. The previous "3+ zeros → rotate" rule was too strict; the agent held D through 8 straight zeros and it eventually paid off on Day 30.
- The drought length is variable: 6 zeros before Day 20 hit, 8 zeros before Day 30 hit. Plan for patience.
- C's Day 28 test is inconclusive. If D continues at ~1/6, a second C test on a Monday (urgency + new-week framing) remains a reasonable fallback.
- A is still unproven. No trigger to test yet.
- Unsubscribe threshold set at 8+ total to pull back on D's tone. Currently at 4; list grew Day 26. No deliverability complaints.

**Next-cycle plan:**
- Continue leading with D. Accept 5–8 zeros between hits as normal.
- Do not rotate off D for short streaks alone. Rotate only if D hits 10+ consecutive zeros (would suggest a structural shift, not just variance).
- Second C test: schedule for a Monday if D stalls past 10 zeros or if purchase-intent signals appear.
- A: revisit only after C has been tested twice.
- Monitor unsubscribes against the 8-total threshold.

**Send window:** 10am daily, confirmed reliable.

**Campaign Working Notes (as of Day 40)**

**Pooled result:** 5 of last 10 pushes landed (up from 3 on Day 30, 4 on Day 20). Clear upward trend across the three reporting windows. Day 40 explicitly: D (+0.50). Four additional hits distributed across Days 31–39 with no per-day breakdown.

**Angle performance, Days 31–40:**
- D (testimonial): 9 pushes (Days 31–35, 37–40). Day 40 confirmed hit. At least 4 of the 5 window hits are D. Cumulative D: 25 pushes, 7 hits ≈ 28%.
- C (urgency): 1 push (Day 36, Monday — the scheduled second test). Outcome not individually confirmed. If C contributed to the 5/10, it would be C's first ever hit (3 pushes, 1 hit). If not, C remains 0/3.
- A, B: No pushes this window. Unchanged from prior.

**Key takeaways:**
- Hit frequency has roughly doubled vs. the Day 21–30 window. Possible drivers: list growth (steady signups, Days 31 & 35), accumulated D reps building familiarity, or variance. Hard to isolate without per-day data.
- The "hold through drought" strategy validated in principle (Day 40 hit after long D streak), but the current hit rate is well above the 1/6–1/8 expectation that formed the patience rule.
- C's Monday test is the critical unresolved question. If C produced a hit, urgency + new-week framing may be a viable secondary angle.
- Legal signed off all four angles (Day 38) — no compliance friction going forward.
- No deliverability complaints. Unsubscribes not reported; assume below threshold.

**Next-cycle plan:**
- Continue D as primary. The elevated hit rate may be temporary; do not reduce cadence based on one window.
- Await per-day breakdown to confirm C's Day 36 result. If C hit, consider a 2-per-week D/C split.
- If C did not hit, park C for now; no further tests until a structural reason emerges.
- A and B remain parked indefinitely absent new evidence.
- Monitor for unsubscribes at the 8-total threshold.

**Send window:** 10am daily, confirmed reliable.

**Campaign Working Notes (as of Day 50)**

**Pooled result:** 4 of last 10 pushes landed (down from 5 on Day 40). Still well above the 1/6–1/8 baseline. Three-window trend: 4 → 5 → 4. Elevated but cooling slightly.

**Angle performance, Days 41–50:**
- D (testimonial): 10 pushes, 4 hits = 40% in this window. Cumulative D: 35 pushes, 11 hits ≈ 31%.
- C (urgency): 0 pushes this window. Day 36 result is now permanently unobservable — it has fallen out of the rolling 10-push window. C remains 3 pushes, 0 confirmed hits.
- A, B: No pushes. Unchanged.

**Key takeaways:**
- The 4/10 dip is modest and likely variance. D's cumulative rate (31%) is the strongest it's been. Do not read one window as a signal to change course.
- C's Day 36 result is unrecoverable. Treat C as 0/3 unless a future report retroactively surfaces it. No further urgency tests scheduled.
- Design refreshed banner art around Day 45. No measurable lift attributable to it yet (the 4/10 could include the first few post-refresh pushes), but no harm either.
- List continues to grow (signups noted Day 49). Familiarity compounding hypothesis remains plausible.
- No deliverability complaints. Unsubscribes not reported.

**Next-cycle plan:**
- Continue D as sole daily angle. No structural reason to deviate.
- C is now effectively parked. Revisit only if a new structural reason emerges (e.g., seasonal urgency event).
- A and B remain parked indefinitely.
- Watch for unsubscribes at the 8-total threshold.
- If hit rate drops to 2–3/10 in a future window, reconsider cadence or angle.

**Send window:** 10am daily, confirmed reliable.

**Campaign Working Notes (as of Day 60)**

**Pooled result:** 4 of last 10 pushes landed (Day 60 report). Same as the prior window. Three-window trend: 4 → 5 → 4 → 4. Stable at 4/10, well above the 1/6–1/8 baseline.

**Angle performance, Days 51–60:**
- D (testimonial): 10 pushes, all queued. No per-day breakdown available. Cumulative D: 45 pushes, 11+ hits ≈ 24–31% (exact count uncertain due to pooled reporting).
- A, B, C: 0 pushes. Parked.

**Unsubscribes:**
- Day 51: 2 processed (total 2)
- Day 53: 2 processed (total 4)
- Day 59: 2 processed (total 6)
- Threshold is 8 total. Two more would trip it. Watch closely next cycle.

**Other signals:**
- List continues to grow (signups noted Days 52, 54, 57). Familiarity compounding hypothesis still plausible.
- No deliverability complaints (Day 58 confirmed).
- Legal signed off on all four angles (Days 55, 56, 60). No compliance risk.
- Banner art refresh from ~Day 45 still shows no measurable lift or harm.

**Key takeaways:**
- 4/10 is now the steady state, not a dip. The earlier "cooling" concern was overblown — it's flat, not declining.
- Unsubscribes are climbing at ~2 per window. At this rate, threshold (8) is roughly 2 pushes away. This is the most actionable risk right now.
- D remains the correct angle. No structural reason to deviate.

**Next-cycle plan:**
- Continue D as sole daily angle.
- **Priority:** Monitor unsubscribes each day. If 2 more arrive (total 8), pause and assess before resuming.
- If hit rate drops to 2–3/10, reconsider cadence or angle.
- A, B, C remain parked indefinitely.

**Send window:** 10am daily, confirmed reliable.
